If you only remember one thing. China's Moonshot released Kimi K three point one Pro. Independent rankings put it fourth overall. And free open weights are due by November fourth.

Section one. A I models.

Moonshot A I launched Kimi K three point one Pro, with a one million token context window. Artificial Analysis ranks it number four on its intelligence index. That's ahead of Open A I's G P T six Astra, and behind only Anthropic's Opus five point five and Sonnet five point five pair, and Meta's Muse Wonder. It costs about two dollars in and ten dollars out per million tokens. That's roughly a fifth of Astra's price. It also scores sixty four percent as a cyber defense model, with no safety refusals.

Why it matters. A free Chinese model now sits near the top, which pressures U S labs to ship their next releases.

Also today. Canva launched Craft, its first in house image model. It debuted at number four on Design Arena. Mini Max released M three point one Flash at very low prices. And Deep Seek open sourced its inference framework.

Why it matters. Cheaper, faster models are arriving from many directions at once.

Section two. Tech geopolitics and chips.

Deep Seek reportedly raised about fifteen billion dollars, backed by Tencent and C A T L. Meanwhile, Washington barred Deep Seek products from federal civilian systems. Byte Dance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly ordered over three million export compliant Nvidia workstation chips. But Nvidia may not be able to fill them all. And China's proposed A I export controls are open for comment until November fifteenth.

Why it matters. Export rules are shaping what chips and models cross borders, in both directions.

Section three. A I policy and jobs.

China's State Council issued guidance with eighteen tasks. It pairs A I job creation with support for displaced workers, including gig workers. It also calls for early warning systems for job market disruption.

Why it matters. Beijing is building employment policy into A I adoption from the start.

Section four. Creative rights.

From your Reads. A D C Creative Rights Salon debated who owns style, voice and likeness. The framing was three questions. What a model learns from. What it generates. And your own face and voice. Each needs a different remedy. The proposed federal No Fakes Act is still pending.

Why it matters. The law is clear as mud, and comms and media people will feel it first.

Section five. Good news and a practical tip.

A guide in your Rundown shows how to let an A I agent sign in using one password approval, without ever pasting a password into chat. And Ant Group released a healthcare focused model that anyone can build on.

Why it matters. Safer agent logins make A I helpers less risky to use.

Also in your Reads. The New Yorker daily covers Meta's work on school safety. And Washington Business Journal has local business news. Readwise wasn't connected today, so no saves were included.

The thread. Open models and chips are the story. Who builds them, who can buy them, and who writes the rules.

That's your briefing. Have a great day.
